As an environmentally supportive institution, the HKMA's carbon reduction strategy will continue to evolve to reflect the latest developments in markets, regulations, technology, and other climate-related factors. To further strengthen the HKMA's climate resilience and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of using technology solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our office. Additionally, we will continue to actively encourage employee participation in our sustainability efforts, including launching campaigns to cultivate sustainable habits and optimizing office processes and practices. Furthermore, the HKMA will maintain a consistent, efficient, and sustainable procurement approach, including assessing suppliers' ESG practices when selecting and renewing contracts. Building on the green data center certification obtained in 2023, the HKMA commits to upholding specified certification standards. For regular updates to data center facilities, in addition to keeping pace with the latest technological developments, we will also incorporate green design and practices. At the same time, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through technology application and consolidation, and actively modernize internal systems to enhance efficiency and minimize potential risks. Finally, in terms of social focus areas, the HKMA will identify more community service opportunities for colleagues, collaborate with the industry to promote financial inclusion and enhance financial literacy, and raise public awareness of financial fraud prevention.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainable development organisation, contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and the broader Asian region. The HKMA has established a robust sustainable development governance framework to lead the formulation of relevant strategies and policies, oversee the implementation of measures, and ensure the integration of sustainable development factors into its own operations and practices. Committed to good institutional governance, the HKMA has built a sound sustainable development governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency. This governance framework ensures the effective integration of sustainable development factors into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and includes effective mechanisms to monitor and evaluate the progress and effectiveness of sustainable development efforts. The HKMA's sustainable development governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and relevant specialised committees, which oversee and advise on the HKMA's work, including its sustainable development efforts; the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, which leads the overall environmental, social, and governance (ESG) strategy and policy at the management level; in responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office coordinates and supervises ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and for other functional areas, relevant groups and task forces plan and execute sustainable development measures related to banking, market development, and the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-founded by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the work of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other parties to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion of the HKMA's sustainable development work in recent years, we established the Steering Committee in October as a new central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainable development efforts across the HKMA's different functional areas¹. It provides guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans for ESG-related matters in four functional areas: banking, market development, Exchange Fund investment, and internal operations; oversees the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's functional departments; evaluates the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG goals; and supervises external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, with three Deputy Chief Executives as permanent members. Additionally, we invite dedicated Assistant Chief Executives from key functions related to green and sustainable development to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on key achievements and future plans of their work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's Banking Department, Institutional Development and Operations Department, External Department, and Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainable development measures, the HKMA co-founded the Steering Group with the SFC in May 2020². As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral work on climate and environmental risks in the financial industry, aiming to strengthen Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and globally. For details on the Steering Group's work, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem."

Climate change is a significant risk facing the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening Hong Kong's financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related matters in their daily business operations. To continue playing their vital role in the financial system and channel more funds into green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risks. As the banking regulator, the HKMA focuses particularly on building banks' capacity to address and manage climate risks, and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. The HKMA is dedicated to formulating various policy measures to enhance the banking system's resilience to climate risks. In August, the HKMA issued a circular on net-zero transition planning, outlining high-level principles to help banks maintain safety and soundness during the economic transition to net-zero emissions. Following this circular, we conducted a questionnaire survey on some banks in Q4 to understand their transition planning measures. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices on transition planning with the industry and hold seminars or workshops to facilitate experience exchange. On disclosure requirements, in response to the latest international developments, including the International Financial Reporting Sustainability Disclosure Standards announced in June and the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's (BCBS) consultation in November on the third-pillar disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks, the HKMA is strengthening its efforts to enhance the sustainability-related disclosure framework for Hong Kong banks. Specifically, the HKMA is collaborating with local authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong that aligns with the International Financial Reporting Sustainability Disclosure Standards. During the year, the HKMA strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and provided advice to help banks further improve their climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. The HKMA made significant progress in implementing a two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process. Climate risk management has now been included as a standing agenda item in prudential supervision meetings with bank management. Banking supervisors have also adopted an enhanced CAMEL rating system that incorporates climate risk factors to assess banks' risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of the implementation of the two-year plan to integrate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process, the HKMA revised the "green" assessment framework to focus on banks' transition planning measures. The HKMA is also reviewing the Supervisory Review Process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with a view to encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks to address climate risks. Key work priorities under the two-year plan in 2023: Following the end of the 12-month implementation period for compliance with the Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management," the HKMA conducted a thematic review on climate-related risk governance in Q2. This review covered four major areas: governance structure for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategy, oversight of climate risk management, and institutional culture, awareness, and communication. The HKMA made several improvements to the climate risk stress testing framework, including introducing a new 5-year scenario to assess the potential impact of simultaneous economic and climate change shocks on banks. Following these improvements, and as part of the HKMA's regular regulatory-led stress testing programme, the second round of climate risk stress testing commenced in June to conduct a comprehensive assessment of banks' climate risk exposures and further enhance banks' ability to manage climate risks. A total of 44 banks participated in this stress test, an increase of over 60% compared to the first pilot exercise in 2021. The HKMA also held a climate risk stress testing forum in November, attended by up to 300 banking practitioners. By facilitating experience sharing among banks, this event helped deepen the industry's overall understanding of climate risk measurement. The HKMA also conducted a series of consultation meetings to review banks' progress in implementing the HKMA's Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management." The HKMA held meetings with bank management to discuss their work on climate risk management and common challenges faced by the industry, and reviewed information provided by banks and other public information to assess their relevant progress. The HKMA provided targeted advice to banks, encouraging and supporting them to continue strengthening their climate risk management capabilities in line with the HKMA's supervisory expectations. As global attention on climate change increases and efforts to address the issue intensify, the HKMA has noted a growing demand for green and sustainable investment products, with some banks offering such products to meet customer needs. In response, the HKMA completed a thematic review of banks' sale of green and sustainable investment products and issued a circular in November outlining the standards the HKMA expects banks to meet and sharing observed good practices. This circular covers areas such as product due diligence, disclosure, governance and controls, staff training, and bookkeeping, aiming to reduce potential greenwashing risks and enhance investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of such investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The HKMA is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For example, technology can improve data availability and risk analysis, strengthening banks' ability to manage climate risks. The HKMA will soon launch a pilot version of a cloud platform for banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. Additionally, the HKMA continues to collaborate with other central banks and regulatory bodies to explore how technological solutions can assist in physical risk assessment. On another front, the HKMA encourages the adoption of sustainable anti-money laundering (AML) practices through advanced analytics and artificial intelligence, reducing the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the HKMA launched an online shared data submission platform to fully automate the collection of financial crime risk data, thereby strengthening banks' sustainable submission of AML-related data. In September, the HKMA hosted the "Green Fintech Competition" to seek market-ready solutions to help the banking sector address challenges in the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted over 85 entries from approximately 70 companies. In December, the HKMA held the "Green and Sustainable Banking Seminar," providing a platform for the banking sector and technology industry to explore the role of low-carbon technology and green fintech in the net-zero transition of Hong Kong and Mainland China. The results of the "Green Fintech Competition" were also announced at the event. The seminar attracted around 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulatory bodies, and academia. To enhance transparency among financial markets and align green and sustainable financial decision-making, the HKMA, with the assistance of a consultant, developed a local green classification framework. In May, the HKMA published a discussion paper on the "Prototype of a Green Classification Framework for Hong Kong," seeking stakeholder views on establishing and implementing a green classification taxonomy. Based on the consultation results, the HKMA is fine-tuning the prototype framework and identifying other areas for the next phase of framework development. The HKMA participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), which has recognised environmental crime as a predicate offence for money laundering. Given the connection between AML and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) considerations, this area is attracting more attention from regulatory bodies. The HKMA recognises the potential risks climate change poses to the financial system and therefore includes a broader range of climate factors and scenarios in its financial risk analysis and research to enhance current monitoring efforts. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analysis of climate-related risks in its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenarios Design and Analysis Working Group of the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helps further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulatory bodies to better understand the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participates in analysing the interaction between transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, allowing policymakers to develop a forward-looking and dynamic perspective on climate-related financial risks. On research, the HKMA has conducted several applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial industry and the economy. Research topics include climate risk exposures of the banking sector and investment funds, ESG fund flows, the impact of climate change on property prices, and the ripple effects of corporate ESG performance in global supply chains. The findings of these studies have enhanced the HKMA's understanding of the impact of climate change and ESG issues on financial stability, aiding in policy formulation. Domestically, these studies help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of climate risk impacts on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA shares its research findings with a broad range of stakeholders through international events on climate-related matters and various channels such as the HKMA Research Memorandums. The HKMA's "Liquidity Facilities Framework" is a secured standby liquidity arrangement providing timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework, as recommended by the NGFS. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and promoting sustainable finance as a mainstream practice. Through this engagement, the HKMA helps facilitate policy dialogue at the international and regional levels on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, gaining insights to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. During the year, the HKMA worked closely with local and international partners to build a richer ecosystem and promote the further development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-led by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the financial industry's response to climate and environmental risks, accelerates the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supports the government's climate strategy. The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced key measures to support Hong Kong in seizing sustainable finance opportunities, with main work areas including sustainable disclosure, ecosystem enhancement, transition finance, and green fintech. Specifically, a Sustainable Disclosure Working Group has been established to develop a roadmap for Hong Kong's adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. The roadmap will cover four key areas: sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. A Transition Finance Working Group has also been set up to explore ways to support financial institutions and corporates in transition planning and reporting. The Steering Group is also strengthening the sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sector skills training and data enhancement. Particularly in data, we continue to promote the adoption of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies 2, launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Steering Group will continue to keep abreast of the latest developments in the green and sustainable finance field and enhance Hong Kong's status as a regional and global green and sustainable finance hub. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced three new key workstreams to capture investment and financing opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region. To facilitate skills training in the industry, the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance under the Steering Group implemented the government's "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme", providing subsidies for practitioners, students, and graduates who undergo green and sustainable finance-related training and obtain relevant qualifications. As of December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training programmes or qualifications were registered as eligible under the scheme, and over 560 subsidy applications were approved. The HKMA also launched the basic level of a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework". This module aims to promote talent development in the banking industry and enhance the overall professional competence of practitioners. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to work with the banking industry to develop the professional level of this module to meet the rapidly growing demand for green and sustainable finance professionals in the industry. To help financial institutions and corporates, especially SMEs, better understand key climate and sustainability-related issues, including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions calculation, and transition planning, the HKMA collaborated with relevant government bureaux and departments, as well as global partners such as CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ)3, and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF)4, to organise a series of seminars and thematic workshops during the year, attracting participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. For students, following the launch of the "Sustainable Finance Internship Programme" in 2022, training courses were held in January and February 2023 to deepen interns and university bachelor's degree graduates' understanding of sustainable finance. Recognising the potential of technology in filling climate-related data gaps and improving data quality, the HKMA is committed to making such data more accessible and improving its quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group launched a series of website enhancement measures to provide one-stop green and sustainable finance information for financial institutions, corporates, and the public. Key enhancements include a sustainable disclosure electronic platform, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and estimation tools, and more centralised, easy-to-navigate, and searchable data and resources. During "Hong Kong Green Week", the Steering Group, together with Cyberport and InvestHK, co-organised the "Leveraging Technology to Catalyse Sustainable Finance" event, showcasing leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong's strengths in green technology. "Hong Kong Green Week – Finance Theme" was held from 26 February to 1 March 2024, attracting over 1,600 guests from nearly 30 regions, including representatives from financial institutions, corporates, central banks, international organisations, government agencies, academia, and consulting firms. The highlight of "Hong Kong Green Week" was the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum" co-organised by the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation. The forum brought together over 400 guests, including top global business and finance decision-makers, to discuss solutions for unlocking climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. The two-day event covered a wide range of topics, including energy transition, heavy industry decarbonisation, circular economy, the future of sustainable finance, and new climate technologies in emerging and developing markets in the Asia-Pacific region. The forum received responses from public and private institutions, co-organising over 10 roundtables, seminars, and other networking events. Topics covered included climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, net-zero transition financing, green finance taxonomy, and green development financing in the Belt and Road region. In addition, the HKMA and the International Monetary Fund co-hosted the "Asia Climate Finance Roundtable" on 29 February 2024, discussing key measures to scale up climate finance and the role of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. These activities are part of the HKMA's overall efforts to promote and enrich Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance ecosystem, serving as useful platforms to help participants drive new business development, share knowledge, and explore new opportunities to address climate finance challenges in the Asia-Pacific region. The HKMA has also been actively supporting green and sustainable finance development in the region. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation and the HKMA launched the "Green Commercial Banking Alliance"5 as a collaborative platform bringing together financial institutions, banking industry organisations, research institutions, and innovative technology providers in the region to jointly develop green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has held 22 training events and roundtables, attracting over 7,300 participants from around the world, including the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. In October, the Alliance, together with Crédit Agricole CIB, published its second cutting-edge research report titled "Developing Ambitious Climate Strategies in Green Banking: Case Studies". During the year, the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the newly established "Coalition for Capacity Building on Sustainable Investment" (CASI) and the "Green Development Investment and Financing Partnership" (GIFP) initiated by the International Coalition for Green Development on the Belt and Road. Collaboration with CASI and GIFP will help build capacity and share knowledge, and channel more funds to green and sustainable projects in Asia and beyond. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of a Hong Kong chapter, which will help support the net-zero efforts of financial institutions in Hong Kong and Mainland China. The HKMA assists GFANZ's work in an advisory capacity. To demonstrate the government's commitment to combating climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018. The HKMA assists in issuing green bonds under the programme. To date, the government has issued approximately US$25 billion equivalent in green institutional and retail bonds, with proceeds allocated to over 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, and energy efficiency and conservation. To enhance the programme's transparency and accountability, the government publishes an annual "Green Bond Report", detailing the allocation of green bond proceeds and expected environmental benefits. The government continued its regular green institutional bond issuance in the 2023-24 fiscal year, issuing approximately US$6 billion equivalent in green bonds in June. This three-currency issuance covered bonds of different tenors in US dollars, euros, and renminbi, attracting various types of investors with strong subscription demand, recording nearly US$30 billion equivalent in subscriptions. The issuance amount of renminbi bonds increased from RMB 10 billion in January to RMB 15 billion, with the first addition of a 10-year renminbi bond, helping to extend the government's renminbi yield curve and further enrich offshore renminbi product options. The strong response from global investors to the government's green bond issuance reflects their recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the government issued a second batch of HKD 20 billion in green retail bonds, further promoting market development and financial inclusion. This issuance provided citizens with a stable-return investment opportunity, allowing them to participate in and benefit from Hong Kong's green finance development.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA plays a key role in promoting green and sustainable finance to support the global climate agenda. The HKMA has been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, the HKMA has been leading green and sustainable asset investment, requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise asset ownership and integrate environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "preservation of capital first, long-term growth"1, believing that due attention to ESG factors helps reduce related investment risks while unlocking long-term sustainable investment value. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and set a "2050 Net Zero" target for its "Investment Portfolio"2, the HKMA is committed to continuously advancing its responsible investment journey, emphasising sustainability, particularly the urgent issue of climate change, aiming to enhance the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieve better risk-adjusted long-term returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA participates in building a robust green and sustainable financial ecosystem, partnering with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to establish industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment in the financial and central banking sectors. Through stewardship and collaborative measures, the HKMA is dedicated to fostering a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. Figure 1 The Exchange Fund's Responsible Investment Journey Comprehensive and reliable ESG information is crucial for integrating sustainability and planning a credible climate transition to achieve net-zero goals. In fulfilling its commitments to the Glasgow Declaration3 of the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) and the strategic plan of the Cross-Agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance, the HKMA has prepared this chapter on the responsible investment of the Exchange Fund in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The primary guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practice responsible investment while balancing the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, oversees ESG and climate-related risks associated with Exchange Fund investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors implementation through regular reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, coordinates and monitors all ESG work of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Motions and work progress discussed at the quarterly ESG Committee meetings are reported to the Chief Executive of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Additionally, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive and attended by the Chief Executive and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets semi-annually to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG goals. Figure 2 Responsible Investment Governance Structure of the Exchange Fund Investment Office As shown in Figure 1, the Exchange Fund Investment Office began its responsible investment journey in 2016, initially focusing on managing ESG risks that could affect the financial performance of the Exchange Fund. As sustainability rapidly evolved and became a strategic priority for major institutions globally, beyond just risk considerations, the Exchange Fund Investment Office revisited its approach to responsible investment. July 2023 marked another milestone, with the Exchange Fund Investment Office establishing a new Business Strategy Division led by the Chief Strategy Officer, responsible for coordinating and leading the strategic development of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, and incorporating the former Responsible Investment Team under the Risk Management and Monitoring Division—now known as the Sustainable Investment Team. This strategic move reflects the HKMA's shift in focus for responsible investment from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing sustainability-related matters in investments. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with various teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office on ESG integration and assists senior management in managing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across different investment types: Public Market Investments—The Credit, Regulation and Monitoring Committee, composed of senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with input from the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG profile of fixed income portfolios through regular reports from the Risk Management and Monitoring Division. Additionally, the Sustainable Investment Team participates in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers for equity portfolios from an ESG perspective (see "Promoting Active Exercise of Asset Ownership" in the "Risk Management" section on page 40). Private Market Investments—The Investment Committee, chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, considers ESG-related assessments for each investment proposal made by the Private Markets Investment and Risk Management teams. The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks4, as well as related opportunities, arising from climate change can affect the long-term performance and value of Exchange Fund investments. The United Nations Environment Programme's "Emissions Gap Report 2023"5 projects that unless global greenhouse gas emissions are further reduced, the global average temperature could rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels by 2030. The urgent need for more aggressive policies, technological developments or behavioural changes to control temperature rise may exacerbate transition risks such as asset devaluation or stranded asset impacts. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events pose additional physical risks to investments. The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in ESG integration. In 2022, the HKMA set a target for the "Investment Portfolio" of the Exchange Fund to achieve net-zero emissions by or before 2050, further demonstrating its commitment to the global climate agenda. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three-pronged approach, with a clear focus on decarbonisation and transition. The following sections will elaborate on this approach. Figure 3 The HKMA's Three-Pronged Approach to Responsible Investment In progressing towards the net-zero target, the HKMA prefers active engagement over exclusion or divestment from its investable universe. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial for achieving the primary investment objective of the Exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially impacting investment returns and risks. An inclusive approach allows the HKMA to seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition, including those in high-emission industries, that possess excellent technology and good corporate governance to navigate evolving global climate trends. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Simply excluding such investments or divesting does not help solve the carbon emission problem. Instead, by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising asset ownership, the HKMA supports these industries, driving their transition to sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby bringing about positive change for themselves and the world. In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net-zero investment strategy, adopting a comprehensive approach to achieve transition outcomes aligned with the Exchange Fund's and global net-zero targets, while adhering to its guiding principles for responsible investment. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities to promote climate transition and enhance the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's asset portfolio (Figure 4). The HKMA's responsible investment maintained good momentum in 2023. In public markets, the HKMA launched a new active global equity portfolio with a sustainability and climate transition theme, managed by an external investment manager, and expanded the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to another portfolio managed by an external investment manager. Furthermore, the HKMA prioritised investments in green, social and sustainability bonds, which outperformed their investment benchmarks, demonstrating the concept of "doing good while doing well". In private markets, the HKMA actively built a resilient long-term growth portfolio, capturing investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic trends such as climate and energy transition. For example, during the year, the HKMA invested in two Asia-focused transition investment funds, reflecting its commitment to addressing Asia's climate transition needs. Figure 4 Ongoing Implementation of Measures to Promote ESG Investments The HKMA has invested in a company that produces environmentally friendly thermoplastic materials from unsorted municipal solid waste (including organic matter such as food waste) and non-recyclable materials. Unlike traditional chemical recycling systems that rely on energy-intensive high-temperature processes to produce plastics, this company has pioneered a low-temperature production method powered entirely by solar arrays. This 100% waste-derived plastic material serves as a sustainable and versatile alternative to oil-based resins commonly used in industries such as retail and consumer durables. Additionally, this plastic material is compatible with existing standard manufacturing processes and cutting-edge technologies like 3D printing. The company is firmly committed to the circular economy. The HKMA committed US$1 billion each to two tranches of the MCPP in 2017 and 2019, and further collaborated with the IFC in 2021 to create a new global climate-related investment platform, "MCPP One Planet", which is also the world's first cross-sector emerging market loan portfolio aligned with the Paris Agreement. Through the MCPP programme, the HKMA has committed to providing loans to 80 sustainable development projects across 19 sectors, including infrastructure, agriculture, real estate and manufacturing, in 38 developing countries. The IFC has collected data on MCPP loans. According to the IFC's report, the HKMA's loan commitments support emerging markets and developing countries in various areas such as economic transformation and human resource development. Specifically, projects financed by the HKMA's loans are expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 5.6 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent annually, equivalent to the greenhouse gases emitted by a typical petrol car travelling 14 billion miles. The HKMA is committed to becoming a sustainable institution, adopting a multi-pronged approach to reduce its carbon footprint, with a target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA also focuses on employee well-being and social responsibility, and strives to promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy. As a responsible institution, the HKMA has set sustainability goals under the three pillars of environment, employees, and social responsibility. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee)¹, established in October and chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, is the primary decision-making body for the institution's sustainability initiatives. The predecessor of the Steering Committee was the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, which was responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating the vision, strategy, and policies for institutional sustainability and social responsibility matters. At the departmental level, the Deputy Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and regularly submits progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Service Team provide support for coordinating the institution's sustainability efforts; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming on how to create a green working environment, while the latter aims to foster a culture of volunteer participation. The HKMA has developed a roadmap to guide its transformation journey. Key focus areas include implementing carbon reduction strategies in its daily operations, such as operating green buildings and data centres, practising green commuting, adopting energy-saving measures, utilising digital tools and more environmentally friendly operational modes, reducing waste, and building a sustainability culture. The HKMA also plans to use carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and employ carbon offsetting measures for emissions that are difficult to reduce. In addition to the above environmental commitments related to its daily operations, the HKMA continues to introduce more environmentally friendly operational solutions for the wider community, covering channels for banks to submit electronic documents and communications, as well as electronic payment and coin collection programmes for the general public. To strengthen and maintain its operational capacity, the HKMA hires a professional workforce, builds a talent pool, and focuses on employee well-being. In terms of social responsibility, the HKMA encourages employees to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; considers the selection of social enterprises in procurement; promotes financial services consumer education; and collaborates with the banking industry to ensure fair access to basic banking services for all sectors of society. The remainder of this chapter details the above strategies. Under the HKMA's overall institutional risk management framework, the Risk Committee², chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, considers potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. The physical impacts of climate change, such as flooding or other damage caused by more extreme weather, could affect the HKMA's offices and impede employee travel. To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its business continuity plans to address extreme weather conditions. The HKMA also conducts regular evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure employees are always prepared to implement business continuity measures. Office designs also incorporate multiple measures to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the HKMA's energy use, air travel, and waste disposal. The HKMA monitors its exposure to transition risks by tracking its greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, and energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions for Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 (air travel) across all operational areas by 2050 or earlier. As a near-term emission reduction target, the HKMA plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions by converting all its existing vehicles to electric vehicles; and, using 2015 as the base year, reduce Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier through various carbon reduction and offsetting strategies. Despite challenges in determining Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will adopt a multi-pronged approach, where practicable, to minimise Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions (e.g., paper consumption, waste generation, and air travel). The HKMA's long-term and near-term emission reduction targets are formulated with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative methodology, which has also been verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA). The HKMA has appointed HKQAA to verify its emissions, energy and paper consumption, and waste data disclosed in this report⁶. The scope and basis of verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing the "2022 Annual Report", the HKMA also independently published its first "2022 Sustainability Report". The HKMA's enhanced ESG reporting efforts were recognised, winning an ESG Award in the "Public Sector Category" at the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023". The HKMA is the first financial regulatory body to receive an award in this category. The judging panel praised the HKMA for achieving good ESG standards, noting that the Sustainability Report was clear and easy to read, and that appointing an independent body to verify its target-setting methodology and environmental data disclosed in the report reflected its commitment to high transparency and accountability in reporting. Furthermore, the HKMA received the highest rating, a Gold Award in the "Non-Profit and Charitable Organisations" category, at the Hong Kong Management Association's "2023 Best Annual Report Awards". The judging panel commended the HKMA's annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial information and making good use of infographics, demonstrating the HKMA's commitment to enhancing financial literacy and promoting financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, employees, and the community at large, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years Plus Caring Company" logo for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to properly managing the environmental impact of its operations. Its internal "Green Office Guidelines" provide guidance to staff on resource use and office waste generation. The HKMA has integrated environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its owned and leased offices. When renovating offices, the HKMA reuses existing furniture and finishing materials as much as possible to reduce waste, and prioritises the use of environmentally friendly building and decorative materials. The HKMA has consistently followed this practice, resulting in its renovated offices at Two International Finance Centre receiving Gold certifications under LEED⁷ and BEAM Plus Interiors⁸ in 2021 and 2022, respectively. Adopting new technologies and making good use of existing technologies to improve energy efficiency remains a key focus for the HKMA. In addition to promoting good practices, such as turning off unnecessary lighting in work areas outside office hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include using LED lighting, motion sensors, setting appropriate air-conditioning temperatures, and optimising energy use in IT network infrastructure. The HKMA's energy consumption has been continuously decreasing, reaching 2.59 megawatt-hours per person⁹ in 2023, a 29.7% decrease from the 2015 baseline (Figure 1). Due to the nature of its daily operations, the HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions primarily come from the consumption of electricity generated from fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuel and electricity was 1.48 tCO₂e per person¹⁰, a 45.2% decrease from 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardising equipment, office software, and meeting facilities, the HKMA also adopts digital tools and technologies, automates and streamlines workflows, and builds a digital working environment to enhance online collaboration within the institution.¹¹ Paperless meetings have become the primary mode of meeting at the HKMA. To further reduce paper consumption and improve efficiency, internal administrative tasks are mainly handled through electronic processes. Furthermore, the HKMA encourages employees to adopt green and digital working modes, replacing paper documents and communications with digital methods. Meanwhile, the implementation of an electronic record-keeping system is underway. These green and digital initiatives have yielded positive results. The HKMA's paper consumption intensity in 2023 was 11.55 kg per person, a significant decrease of 64.8% from 2015 (Figure 3). As most international activities have returned to physical formats following the COVID-19 pandemic, and to promote the development of Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre, it is unavoidable that relevant HKMA staff need to travel overseas for business. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to take direct flights where feasible or combine different business trips when participating in overseas activities. At the institutional level, in 2023, the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO₂e through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. Additionally, the HKMA participated in a carbon offset programme certified under the "Gold Standard"¹² to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; this programme involves waste-to-energy, solar power generation, and providing efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA's procurement process considers sustainability and environmental factors. As part of a comprehensive review of the institution's procurement policies and procedures, the existing practice of procuring green products has been formalised, adhering to the environmental specifications of the government's "Green Procurement List", particularly for the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables. Furthermore, ESG factors and innovative proposals that enhance productivity and efficiency have been incorporated into tender evaluation criteria. At the same time, all suppliers must commit to complying with environmental regulations. Following the "4R" principle—Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle—the HKMA adopts a three-pronged approach to minimise waste generation and manage waste disposal. Additionally, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. Details of the non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various recyclable waste, are set out in the "Performance Summary" section on page 56. In 2023, the HKMA participated for the first time directly in the Lai See Packet Recycling Programme organised by the management company of its office building at the International Finance Centre. Staff handed in approximately 3,000 used but still intact and new-looking lai see packets. These packets were subsequently given to an environmental organisation for distribution to the public for use in the following Lunar New Year. Given that the HKMA's operational and backup data centres are a major component of the institution's overall energy consumption, both data centres have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for existing data centres, achieving optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE)¹³. In 2023, the HKMA's two data centres received "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings, respectively, under the "BEAM Plus Existing Data Centres" assessment guide issued in 2021; the HKMA is the first and only institution in Hong Kong to receive such ratings. Improving the energy efficiency of the two data centres has been a key focus of the technical team. To this end, the team has adopted green designs in renovation works and implemented energy-efficient best practices to lower PUE and achieve related targets, including 24-hour monitoring of the data centres' environmental facilities and continuous improvement of environmental factors such as airflow and temperature settings. As the technical team continuously improves the energy use of the data centres, the HKMA commissioned an external consultant in December 2021 to conduct a review to comprehensively assess the green level of the data centres and formulate recommendations to further enhance performance in various aspects. The study was completed in mid-2022. The HKMA also began preparations shortly after the study's completion to obtain "Green Data Centre" certification under the BEAM Plus certification scheme. The certification process is comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the technical team implemented optimisation measures based on the recommendations of the consultant's report to enhance energy performance and the health elements of the working environment within the data centres.

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) has conducted independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) 2023 environmental data ("2023 Data"). The 2023 Data includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, business air travel greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste) for 2023, their respective intensities, and the changes in these data compared to the 2015 baseline. Additionally, the 2023 Data includes the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the change compared to the level when HKMA launched its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. HKMA's greenhouse gas emission data is prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHG Protocol) jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, and also covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison (excluding food waste). The verification scope covers a total of 5 office and warehouse assets, including 4 offices located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and a warehouse at 5) Luxor Industrial Centre, Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data, and to confirm the adequacy of HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the verification scope, HKQAA reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 5 assets. This verification work was performed in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to obtain a reasonable level of assurance for forming conclusions and opinions. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and performed reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanism, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and checking selected representative data and information. Relevant original data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the data. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The HKQAA verification team did not participate in the preparation process of the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance on the 2023 Data and concludes that: the 2023 Data is materially accurate and reliable; HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shen Xiaoyin Audit Supervisor Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency April 2024

The threat posed by climate change is imminent, making it imperative to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization has confirmed that 2024 was the hottest year on record and the first year in which global temperatures exceeded the critical 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Meanwhile, global greenhouse gas emissions, which had temporarily eased during the COVID-19 pandemic, have recently reached new highs, highlighting the inadequacy of current climate mitigation measures. In the process of addressing global warming, the manifestation of climate-related risks is set to intensify, with unpredictable impacts on the economy and financial markets. Furthermore, the current tense geopolitical landscape, increasingly fragmented global economy, heightened concerns over energy security, and uncertain economic outlook all pose greater challenges for countries in tackling climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. Across the globe, Asia faces the most severe transition challenges. As the World Economic Forum points out, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth but also the region most vulnerable to climate change. Therefore, Asia plays a critical role in the global effort to achieve net-zero emissions. As a leading international financial centre in Asia, Hong Kong must strengthen its leading role by fully leveraging the power of finance to support and drive the regional transition. To this end, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) launched the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" last year, outlining our vision and roadmap for gradually integrating sustainable development principles into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses on two main areas: enhancing the financial industry's capacity to address climate-related risks and assisting the industry in seizing related new opportunities. At the same time, we lead by example. The HKMA's sustainable development efforts encompass four key areas: supporting the banking sector in achieving net-zero emissions, investing in a sustainable future, promoting net-zero financing, and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. The banking system plays a crucial role in the net-zero transition of Hong Kong and Asia, but it also faces significant risks during the transition process. In the "Action Plan," we have set ambitious targets, requiring all banks to strive for net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or earlier and to achieve net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or earlier. We also require all banks to enhance disclosure of climate-related risks and opportunities. While continuously strengthening banks' climate risk management, we provide guidance on transition planning to help them improve their capacity to manage the transition and better handle related risks. We are also working with relevant stakeholders to align Hong Kong's sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, aiming to further enhance transparency in related activities. Additionally, we are refining the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Classification Taxonomy launched in May last year, incorporating more sustainable activities (including transition activities). By providing clear criteria, we aim to channel more funds into sustainable and transition-related projects. Climate change poses significant physical and transition risks that could affect the long-term financial performance and value of the Exchange Fund's investment projects. However, it also presents opportunities for growth and positive impact for the Exchange Fund. Our experience demonstrates that investment returns and positive sustainable impact can be mutually reinforcing, with no inherent conflict. In view of this, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, and in the "Action Plan," we pledged to support Asia's climate transition through the Exchange Fund's investments. Currently, sustainable investments already account for over 10% of the "Investment Portfolio." To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and the International Finance Corporation in November last year, aiming to accelerate the low-carbon economic transition in Asia through co-investments. Furthermore, in September last year, we released the first "HKMA ESG Expectations" document to further encourage fund managers to actively exercise asset ownership and adopt good sustainable investment practices. Financing is particularly crucial for accelerating the regional transition. As an international financial hub and the preferred location for arranging international sustainable bond issuances for Asian issuers (including mainland provincial and municipal governments), Hong Kong plays a vital role in channelling funds to accelerate the regional transition. The "Action Plan" outlines the vision of developing Hong Kong into the region's preferred sustainable development financing platform and the goal of promoting sustainable financial innovation. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" to drive green bond innovation (including the issuance of the world's first multi-currency digital bond in February last year), to expanding the scope of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" to cover transition financing instruments in May last year, and launching the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme" in November last year, we have been consistently encouraging regional issuers to use Hong Kong's financial platform to raise funds needed for decarbonisation and transition. Achieving a robust transition requires not only capital and innovation but also an inclusive and accessible sustainable development ecosystem. This includes reliable sustainable development data, high transparency in information disclosure, and industry talent with relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, we committed in the "Action Plan" to support high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosures and to bridge the gaps in sustainable finance talent and knowledge in the region. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainable disclosures, particularly by providing easy-to-use climate disclosure templates to promote sustainable disclosures among small and medium-sized enterprises. We also launched the "Green and Sustainable Finance" professional-level module under the Banking Professional Qualifications Framework in November last year to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. Additionally, through events such as the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week in February last year and other activities, we have engaged various stakeholders in discussions on sustainable development, fostering collaboration and innovation. Within the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring that our operations align with the vision of sustainable development. In the "Action Plan," we pledged to achieve net-zero emissions in our own operations by 2030 or earlier, advancing our original commitment by 20 years. Furthermore, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainable disclosure standards in accordance with the government's roadmap. We began using electric vehicles in 2024 and have incorporated low-carbon emissions as a screening factor in our procurement processes. At the same time, we continue to enhance work efficiency through digitalisation, foster a culture of sustainable development within the organisation, and motivate employees to actively participate in sustainable development efforts. Multilateral cooperation has always been the cornerstone of global climate action, but the reshaping of the international landscape and dramatic geopolitical changes have added uncertainties to global climate efforts. However, climate change is an undeniable reality that is progressively intensifying. In addressing climate change, the current situation leaves no room for complacency. We firmly believe that promoting an orderly and inclusive transition will help mitigate the impact of climate risks on Hong Kong's financial system and bring us opportunities in the process. As we enter 2025, we will continue to forge ahead, diligently advancing sustainable development efforts and deepening relationships with like-minded partners. Despite the severe challenges, we remain committed to supporting the building of a sustainable future for Hong Kong, Asia, and beyond.

Climate change is a major challenge of our generation. As an international financial centre and a hub for sustainable finance in Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development in Asia and globally. In October 2024, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), outlining the HKMA's vision in this area, including our future direction, timelines for achieving various targets, and how we expect the industry to work together to advance related efforts. The HKMA plans to strengthen the resilience of Hong Kong's financial industry and the HKMA itself against climate change risks, and promote the transition to a more sustainable economy in Asia, through formulating strategic policies, enhancing regulatory engagement, and improving internal operations. By actively participating in international and regional discussions, the HKMA also aims to exert influence in shaping green and sustainable finance policies and standards at the regional and global levels. As a banking regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the climate resilience of the banking sector and supporting banks in maintaining safety and soundness during the transition to net-zero emissions. Our priorities for 2025 include: - Conducting a new round of thematic review on banks' climate risk management practices and holding a third round of consultation meetings to review banks' implementation of the HKMA's relevant regulatory requirements and further strengthen banks' climate risk management capabilities; - Refining the integration of climate risk stress testing into the HKMA's supervisory-led stress testing framework; - Continuing to advance the incorporation of climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review process; - Commencing preparatory work for formulating regulatory requirements on the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's forthcoming Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks and the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) for the local banking industry; - Completing the preparation of the new module GS-2 of the Supervisory Policy Manual, providing guidance to banks on transition planning; and - Sharing good practices with the industry on climate risk management and the application of green fintech. In addition to its role as a banking regulator, the HKMA also acts as a facilitator, committed to promoting the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the transition. We have released the first phase of the "Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Classification Taxonomy", providing the industry with a tool to identify green and sustainable economic activities and facilitate related capital flows. The HKMA has commenced the second phase of the taxonomy to expand its coverage, including adding transition elements, increasing green economic activities, and incorporating climate adaptation objectives. Furthermore, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will organise another green fintech event in 2025 to promote banks' adoption of green fintech solutions. Hong Kong is well-positioned to support sustainable financing needs in the region. To consolidate this role, we will continue to assist the government in implementing the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme", whose expanded scope will include sustainable projects, such as social responsibility projects. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and serve as a demonstration effect for other potential issuers in the region. Additionally, we will continue to provide subsidies through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" to encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong's financing platforms to raise sustainable funds. We will also step up promotional efforts to encourage more governments, institutions, and enterprises from the Mainland and other regions to raise green funds in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including providing subsidies to potential issuers of digital green bonds through the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme". Although market demand for high-quality sustainable disclosures by institutions and enterprises is increasing, different entities have varying capabilities and readiness in making sustainable disclosures, and some may require additional guidance and support. In view of this, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to make sustainable disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their clients with more climate disclosure-related tools, including easy-to-use sustainable disclosure templates and supporting tools; explore how to leverage technology to further enhance the user-friendliness of existing resources; and collaborate with key local industry organisations to provide necessary training for the industry. The rapidly evolving sustainable finance market requires expanding the local talent pool and filling knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and the region. The HKMA's key tasks in 2025 include collaborating with the banking industry to develop professional-level training courses for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework", and identifying areas with further training needs in the industry through the upcoming "Future Banking Talent 2026-2030" study. Additionally, we plan to work with key stakeholders to enhance the promotion of the government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" and review its scope of application. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the "Green Commercial Banking Alliance" to launch special initiatives in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted upskilling and training support, fostering community engagement, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to help banks develop roadmaps to make green finance a core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA commits to achieving net-zero emissions for the "Investment Portfolio" of the Exchange Fund by or before 2050, to support the overall economic transition. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of Exchange Fund investments through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approach, focusing primarily on the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that can promote positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to setting an example in institutional sustainability efforts. In response to the accelerated timeline for achieving net-zero commitments announced in the "Action Plan", the HKMA will progressively incorporate environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessment, and reporting at a pragmatic pace, continuing to drive the institution's sustainability. Specifically, in 2025, we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring we focus on material topics. Additionally, we will conduct an energy audit and use technology solutions to assess the significant impacts of climate risks on our offices and operations, to enhance our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the government's release of the "Hong Kong Sustainable Disclosure Roadmap" and are actively preparing to make disclosures in accordance with the ISSB Standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment to selecting data centres for planned upgrades based on energy efficiency and conservation principles. We will also expand digital initiatives to promote sustainability and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and improving the overall digital experience for our staff, banks, and the public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainable development organisation, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and the broader Asian region. The HKMA has established a robust sustainable development governance framework to lead the formulation of relevant strategies and policies, oversee the implementation of measures, and ensure the integration of sustainable development factors into its own operations and practices. Committed to good institutional governance, the HKMA has built a sound sustainable development governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency. This governance framework ensures the effective integration of sustainable development factors into the HKMA’s strategic planning and decision-making processes, and includes effective mechanisms to monitor and assess the progress and effectiveness of sustainable development efforts. The HKMA’s sustainable development governance framework comprises: - The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and relevant specialist committees, which oversee and advise on the HKMA’s work, including its sustainable development efforts; - The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, which leads the overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategy and policy at the management level; - In the area of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office coordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and - For other functional areas, relevant groups and task forces plan and implement sustainable development measures related to banking, market development, and the HKMA’s own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-founded by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the efforts of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other parties to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion of the HKMA’s sustainable development work over the past years, we established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainable development efforts across the HKMA’s different functional areas. - Providing guidance on the strategy, policy, and planning of ESG-related matters across four functional areas: banking, green and sustainable finance ecosystem development, Exchange Fund investment, and internal operations; - Overseeing the implementation of ESG-related initiatives by the HKMA’s functional departments; - Assessing the HKMA’s performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and - Overseeing external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, with three Deputy Chief Executives as permanent members. Additionally, we invite dedicated Assistant Chief Executives from key functions related to green and sustainable development to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on major achievements and future plans of their work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA’s Banking Department, Institutional Development and Operations Department, External Department, and the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainable development measures, the HKMA co-founded the Steering Group with the SFC in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral work on climate and environmental risks in the financial industry, aiming to strengthen Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For details on the Steering Group’s work, please refer to the chapter “Enhancing the Development of the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem.”

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has been committed to enhancing the resilience of Hong Kong's financial system against climate risks, while contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face various impacts from sustainability and climate-related matters in their daily business operations, and must therefore proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, banks play a crucial role in the financial system by channeling funds towards green and sustainable projects. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to address and manage climate risks, and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. In October, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), outlining the HKMA's vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a regional sustainable finance hub and support sustainable development in Asia and globally. The "Action Plan" includes eight targets across four areas. To assist the industry in achieving the objectives of the relevant banking policies, we have been carrying out the following work. All banks are committed to achieving net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or earlier. All banks are to increase transparency on climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices on transition planning with the industry and initiated an industry consultation on the draft of Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-2 "Transition Planning".
