The new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks' capacity to address net-zero transition and related risk management. Additionally, we are reviewing the Supervisory Review Process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with the aim of incorporating factors proposed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) for effective management of climate-related financial risks into the assessment process, and encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks (including transition planning) to address climate risks. The HKMA has been working to align local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) and the BCBS's Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analyzing the latest developments in sustainability disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on adopting the ISSB Standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the "Action Plan". In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Classification (Taxonomy) to address industry concerns about greenwashing and help guide capital flows towards green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors, aiming to align with common green taxonomies and those of Mainland China and the European Union, while incorporating local elements. We have commenced the second phase of work to expand the scope of the Taxonomy and are consulting a wide range of stakeholders to further facilitate the flow of green and sustainable funds. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and supported banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and address climate change. The HKMA also completed all work under the two-year plan formulated in 2022 to integrate climate risks into the banking supervisory process. To promote banks' capacity to enhance climate risk management, the HKMA shared with the banking industry good practices observed during thematic reviews and consultation meetings, including: - Establishing a robust governance structure with clearly defined responsibilities for the board and senior management - Ensuring effective oversight of key areas of climate-related risk matters (1) Promoting and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) Exercising appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) Fostering a sound climate risk culture within the institution. In August, the HKMA held a balanced supervision roundtable on climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on various climate risk-related topics, including challenges banks face in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning, and finance. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and helped the HKMA in its work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA launched a round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management". The thematic reviews covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The HKMA held a second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new batch of banks in implementing Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" and understand the challenges they face. The consultation meetings also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provided bank-specific feedback and guidance to support their climate risk management efforts. In 2024, the HKMA completed the second round of the Banking Sector Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST), with participation from 21 retail banks and 25 Hong Kong branches of international banking groups. The results showed that under various scenarios (including simultaneous climate risk and macroeconomic downturn assumptions), the Hong Kong banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience against severe climate-related shocks. Compared to the CRST pilot, participating banks significantly improved their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risks. A report detailing the CRST results and good practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025. The HKMA recognizes the numerous challenges banks face regarding data and methodologies in climate risk management, and has therefore been working on various initiatives to promote the use of technology to address these challenges. To address the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risk assessment, the HKMA launched a Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform based on user feedback and by incorporating more local data. Furthermore, the HKMA collaborates with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the broader financial services industry. During the year, we published an application practice guide and two "Compliance Technology Use Case Briefs" (English versions), describing technology solutions for Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) and sustainability assessment, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also held the third "FiNETech", bringing together over 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore green fintech collaboration. The HKMA recognizes that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, and therefore incorporates a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen ongoing monitoring efforts. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its continuous monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analysis of climate-related risks in its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Working Group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helps further enrich climate scenarios, aiding central banks and regulators in understanding the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. In November, the NGFS published the fifth version of long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participates in analyzing the interaction between transition planning of financial and non-financial firms and financial stability, enabling policymakers to take a forward-looking and dynamic perspective on climate-related financial risks. The HKMA published a "Practical Guide for Banks on Applying Green Technology" (English version), providing best practices for financial institutions to leverage green technology to facilitate their net-zero transition. In terms of research, the HKMA conducted several applied research projects exploring the impact of climate change on the financial industry and the broader economy. Research topics included the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in withstanding monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial industry in moving towards a low-carbon economy. The findings of these studies not only enhance our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability but also provide valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, aiding in policy formulation. Locally, these studies help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. The research findings are also shared with a wide range of stakeholders through various channels, including international forums and the "HKMA Research Memoranda". The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (Research Institute), the research arm of the Hong Kong Academy of Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provides evidence that low-emission firms can benefit significantly from carbon pricing and highlights its role in improving efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. The study is included in the Research Institute's "Insights from Monetary Research" and shared with local and international academics and policy researchers. The HKMA's "Liquidity Facilities Framework" is a secured standby funding arrangement providing timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and promoting sustainable finance as a mainstream issue. Through this engagement, we help facilitate policy dialogue at the international and regional levels on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draw lessons to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As articulated in the HKMA's "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), the HKMA is dedicated to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to positioning Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and globally, supporting technological innovation in the green sector of the financial market, enhancing sustainable disclosure in the industry, expanding the local green talent pool, and addressing knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. Positioning Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform in the region and globally Catalysing sustainable finance innovation Supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure Filling the talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in the region To demonstrate the government's determination to tackle climate change, promote green finance, and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the government in issuing approximately USD 28 billion equivalent in green bonds to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds raised have been allocated to over 110 government green projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, and energy efficiency and conservation. We seize each issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currency, tenor, and distribution channels, laying the foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the programme's impact and further consolidate Hong Kong's status as a green and sustainable finance hub, the programme's scope was expanded to cover sustainable projects and was renamed the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" (Sustainable Bond Programme). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the government publishes an annual "Green Bond Report", detailing the allocation of proceeds raised from green bonds and the expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the government in issuing approximately USD 3 billion equivalent in institutional green bonds under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This three-currency issuance covered bonds of different tenors in Renminbi, US dollars, and Euros. These bonds attracted participation from various types of investors, with strong subscription demand, recording over USD 15 billion equivalent in subscription amounts. Among them, the 20-year and 30-year Renminbi green bonds were the government's first issuance of such tenors, representing the longest-tenor Renminbi bonds ever issued by the government, setting a new benchmark for the market and further demonstrating the exemplary role of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also further enriched the range of offshore Renminbi investment products in Hong Kong. Furthermore, the strong response from global investors to the government's green bonds reflects their recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. To encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong's financing platform to raise sustainable development funds, the HKMA continues to implement the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" launched in May 2021, providing subsidies for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The scheme has been well received by the industry. As of the end of 2024, the scheme had approved subsidies for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total value exceeding USD 140 billion. The scheme was extended for three years to 2027 in May 2024, and its scope was expanded to include transition bonds and loans. The purpose of extending and expanding the scheme is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries in the region to use Hong Kong's transition financing platform to gradually decarbonise. - Subsidies approved for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total value exceeding USD 140 billion (as of the end of 2024) - Extended for three years to 2027, with the scope expanded to include transition financing instruments At the same time, the HKMA actively promotes Hong Kong's sustainable financing platform, and these efforts have achieved positive results. Notably, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government issued offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong for the fourth time in August, with a total value of RMB 7 billion, including RMB 2.7 billion in green bonds, RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds, and RMB 0.9 billion in social responsibility bonds. In September, the Guangdong Provincial People's Government issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, with a total value of RMB 5 billion, including RMB 1.5 billion in green bonds. In October, the Hainan Provincial People's Government also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, with a total value of RMB 3 billion, including RMB 1 billion in blue bonds and RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds. These bond issuance activities repeatedly highlight Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating the flow of green and sustainable funds between Mainland China and the rest of the world. Leveraging these measures, Hong Kong has consolidated its position as the preferred platform for sustainable financing in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, in 2024, Hong Kong continued to be the largest hub in Asia for arranging international green and sustainable bond issuances, with a total of USD 43.1 billion in such bonds arranged through Hong Kong, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the government in issuing two landmark tokenised green bonds in 2023 and 2024, respectively the world's first tokenised government green bond and the world's first multi-currency digital bond. These issuances demonstrate the government's support for market participants in the region applying asset digitalisation and innovative technologies in the green and sustainable finance field. The HKMA also launched the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme" in November to promote digital bond issuances in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting innovative development in Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance market. The working group on sustainable disclosure under the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group) has been working on Hong Kong's adoption of the "International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards" (ISSB Standards). The government published the "Hong Kong Sustainability Disclosure Roadmap" in December 2024, providing a clear pathway for large public interest entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards by no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to support entities at different stages of preparation in achieving high-quality sustainable disclosure, making sustainable disclosure more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continue to encourage the application of the "Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies" (Questionnaire) launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template to facilitate sustainable disclosure by enterprises, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024, allowing enterprises to fill it out online (see QR code below). The HKMA is optimising the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to make it more user-friendly. Specific measures include selecting core questions from the Questionnaire and providing common usage scenarios for the Questionnaire. Additionally, we aim to improve the compatibility of the Questionnaire with other supporting tools on the Steering Group's website. For more information on the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage. The HKMA leads by example, making high-quality sustainable disclosures in its "Sustainability Report" in accordance with the latest global standards to demonstrate its commitment. The report contains rich content, including the HKMA's climate-related institutional operational risks, as well as plans and progress towards achieving climate goals. For details on our own operational sustainable disclosures, please refer to the "Sustainable HKMA" chapter. Given the rapidly evolving sustainable finance market, to fill the knowledge and talent gaps, the HKMA is strengthening skills training in the banking industry and promoting knowledge sharing with other regulatory bodies and international stakeholders. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners in sustainable finance, the HKMA, in collaboration with the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB), launched the basic level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework" in July 2023. This module aims to help banking professionals acquire knowledge in green and sustainable finance more effectively and develop relevant professional capabilities, covering four main work areas: (1) Green and sustainable finance products and services; (2) Sustainable/climate risk management; (3) Sustainable disclosure and reporting; and (4) Sustainable strategy, compliance, and governance. Additionally, the professional level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, targeting mid-to-senior level banking practitioners responsible for related work, was launched in November. To provide necessary training for banking practitioners, the HKIB, as the managing body of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, launched the basic level training course for the module in May. Following the launch of the professional level in November, the HKMA will collaborate with the banking industry in 2025 to develop training courses for the professional level. To understand further skills and training needs in the banking industry, the HKMA is currently collaborating with the banking industry on a study on "Future Banking Talent 2026-2030", with the aim of publishing the study results in 2025. This joint study is a follow-up to the "Future Banking Talent 2021-2025" document published in June 2020. The results of the follow-up study will provide important references for the industry, helping to formulate and adjust talent training strategies and measures to support the sustainable development of the banking industry. The HKMA, through its collaboration with the Steering Group, also continues to assist in implementing the government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme", subsidising practitioners, graduates, and students to receive sustainable finance-related training. As of December 2024, the scheme had registered 85 international and local courses as eligible training courses and approved over 5,700 reimbursement applications. The government announced in the "2025-26 Budget" that the scheme will be extended to 2028. The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international cooperation. As a founding member of the "Sustainable Investment Capacity Building Alliance" (CASI), the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-organised a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, with discussions focusing on the global sustainable finance market, policy frameworks, and innovative instruments. Furthermore, the HKMA supports the establishment of a branch office of the "Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero" (GFANZ) in Hong Kong in October and will leverage GFANZ's network and expertise to strengthen skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Leveraging its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can complement each other, the HKMA adheres to a responsible investment philosophy in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritising sustainable assets and requiring its external investment managers to proactively exercise asset ownership. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "preserving capital first, achieving long-term growth", believing that giving due attention to environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate related investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As a firm signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is committed to advancing its responsible investment efforts. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, aiming to enhance the resilience of the Exchange Fund and strive for better risk-adjusted long-term returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment instruments to channel capital into sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1). The HKMA leverages its role as a major investor to contribute to the advancement of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA published the "HKMA ESG Expectations" and made this document publicly available to investment partners through the annual ESG workshop and the HKMA website. We partner with like-minded investors, regulators, and international organisations to jointly develop industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment within the financial industry and central banking community. Through these collaborative efforts, we are committed to fostering a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. In October, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), outlining its commitment to achieving net-zero emissions by or before 2050 through the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" and mobilising partners to support the low-carbon economic transition, further solidifying its commitment to investing in a sustainable future. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The primary guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to balance responsible investment practices with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, oversees ESG and climate-related risks associated with Exchange Fund investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors implementation through regular reports from the Sustainable Investment Group of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, coordinates and monitors all ESG work of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Motions and work progress discussed at the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Additionally, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets regularly to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment Group works closely with various teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office on ESG integration and assists senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across various investment projects: - Public Market Investments – The Credit, Regulation and Monitoring Committee, composed of senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with input from the Sustainable Investment Group, and monitors the ESG status of the fixed income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Monitoring Department. Additionally, the Sustainable Investment Group participates in the selection, appointment, and monitoring process of external investment managers for equity portfolios from an ESG perspective (see "Promoting Active Exercise of Asset Ownership" in the "Risk Management" section on page 39 for details). - Private Market Investments – The Investment Committee, chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, considers ESG-related assessments made by the Private Markets Investment and Risk Management teams for each investment proposal. The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks and related opportunities arising from climate change can affect the long-term financial performance of Exchange Fund investments. The United Nations Environment Programme's "Emissions Gap Report 2024" projects that unless there is a large-scale global mobilisation to rapidly reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the global average temperature will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Uncertainties in policy changes, technological developments, and behavioural shifts in response to rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and affecting asset valuations. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also pose additional risks of physical damage and financial losses to investments. Amid these challenges, governments and industries shifting towards sustainable solutions also create investment opportunities with potentially attractive long-term prospects in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies, and sustainable infrastructure. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in its ESG integration. The HKMA has set a target for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by or before 2050, and continues to advance its work through an orderly three-pronged approach to achieve this goal (see Figure 3). In 2024, the HKMA announced the "Action Plan", which consolidates the Exchange Fund's commitments and efforts related to climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the low-carbon economic transition, the HKMA prefers proactive engagement over exclusion or divestment from investable projects. Investing in a Sustainable Future: Net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by or before 2050 - Actively expand the scope and types of sustainable investments, particularly climate transition-themed investments in public and private markets - Integrate ESG factors into every investment decision, with special attention to climate change and transition prospects - Establish clear ESG expectations aligned with international standards and best practices, and require all external investment managers, investee companies, and counterparties to comply - Commit to reducing the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio by 67% from 2017 levels by or before 2030 Supporting Regional Transition through Investment - Continue to engage with external investment managers to optimise transition-driven investment opportunities - Continue to identify and prioritise high-quality investment opportunities that can facilitate Asia's transition and generate positive global impact First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial to achieving the primary investment objective of the Exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, with potential implications for investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition, including those in high-emission industries, that possess excellent technology and good corporate governance to navigate evolving global climate trends. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Simply excluding related investments or divesting does not help solve the carbon emission problem. Instead, by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising asset ownership, the HKMA supports these industries in transitioning to sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby driving beneficial changes for themselves and the world. The net-zero investment approach has evolved from favouring green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, to drive comprehensive carbon reduction across the entire economy. As a global asset owner, the HKMA understands that the long-term resilience of a portfolio depends not only on the portfolio's own adjustments but also on a broad economic transition. While there is no single perfect solution, the HKMA refined its responsible investment strategy in 2024, adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive transition while supporting the net-zero goals of the Exchange Fund and the world. This strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including integrating ESG factors and stewardship into fundamental analysis, portfolio decarbonisation tilting, and thematic investments in various assets aligned with the path to net-zero emissions. In public markets, this may involve tilting portfolios towards ESG leaders or climate solution providers, coupled with stewardship to drive corporate transition. In private markets, it may place greater emphasis on transition-promoting investments. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continuously identifies investment opportunities that can facilitate climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's portfolio. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio", with financial performance comparable to the relevant portfolio benchmarks (Figure 5). - Public Market Investments – The HKMA launched an active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and expanded the application of customised low-carbon equity indices to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek green, social, and sustainability (GSS) bonds that provide competitive returns while financing sustainable projects (see case study in "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds" section). - Private Market Investments – The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio, seizing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the HKMA actively identifies and reviews investment opportunities that can accelerate the energy transition, including through strategic partnerships with multinational organisations (see examples in "Collaborating to Address Climate Challenges in Asia and Globally" section). - Passive investment portfolios using ESG indices as investment benchmarks - Customised carbon reduction strategies for passive and active quantitative investment portfolios using non-ESG indices as benchmarks - Governance-themed active investment portfolios - Active ESG investment portfolios themed on sustainability and climate transition - Projects with sustainable characteristics, such as renewable energy infrastructure, and green-certified buildings and warehouses - Funds themed on energy transition and decarbonisation in global, Asian, and Global South markets - Green, social, and sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organisation - The "Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program" (MCPP) managed by the International Finance Corporation, focusing on sustainable projects in emerging markets - The "MCPP One Planet" project, providing climate-related investments in emerging markets aligned with the Paris Agreement The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a quasi-government agency. The proceeds from the green bond were allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading aged equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrades encompass optimising monitoring and control systems and pump performance to generate positive environmental benefits from wastewater management, waste reduction, and recycling processes. In addition to ongoing wastewater and sludge treatment, these facilities compost or repurpose dewatered sludge to produce fertiliser, charcoal, cement, and other construction materials, achieving a sludge recovery rate of up to 100%. These facilities also utilise gas generated from the sludge treatment process to power boilers and generate electricity. The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a multilateral development bank. This bond finances multiple projects, including the restoration of a country's canal system. As one of the largest irrigation systems in that country, the canal is designed to divert excess river water to arid regions. The main objective of the project is to repair deteriorating canal linings to prevent leakage, conserve water, improve water use efficiency, and reclaim waterlogged areas. Additionally, the project conducts skills training for local stakeholders to promote the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation techniques, such as micro-irrigation, and sustainable farming methods.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable organisation. In 2024, a key focus of fulfilling this commitment was to advance the target for achieving net-zero emissions in its own operations to 2030, 20 years earlier than originally planned, aligning with the Sustainable Finance Action Plan. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is also committed to fostering staff training and well-being, promoting financial inclusion, and enhancing public financial literacy. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, is the primary decision-making body for various institutional sustainability initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA's commitment to climate change, the Steering Committee approved in October 2024 a new target for the HKMA to achieve net-zero emissions in its own operations by 2030 or earlier, as part of the Sustainable Finance Action Plan (the Action Plan). At the departmental level, the Deputy Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) provides guidance on implementing sustainability measures related to institutional operations, staff well-being, and social engagement, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division serves as the coordinator and central hub for executing, communicating, and reporting on institutional sustainability measures. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Service Team, comprising staff from various operational departments, provide additional support; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming and proposing ideas on creating a green working environment, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of staff participation in volunteer activities. In recognition of the HKMA's commitment to caring for the environment, its staff, and the community at large, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years Plus Caring Company" logo consecutively from 2006 to 2024, for 18 years. The HKMA's sustainability strategy continues to adopt a structure comprising three pillars: Environment, Staff, and Social Responsibility. - Focus on decarbonising and digitalising the HKMA's daily operations, targeting net-zero emissions by 2030 or earlier - Adopt green procurement requirements in line with government guidelines - Promote greener operational solutions to the financial industry and the wider community - Build a positive workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA's strategic objectives - Foster a collaborative, caring, and inclusive working environment that values diversity and strengthens staff sense of belonging - Provide a quality working environment that promotes a healthy lifestyle - Cultivate a culture of caring for the community - Integrate social considerations into procurement procedures and supply chain management - Promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy through consumer education activities The HKMA is concerned about climate change and leads by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced plans to advance the target for achieving net-zero emissions in its own operations to 2030, 20 years earlier than its original commitment, as part of the Action Plan. The HKMA has revised its roadmap for the net-zero transition, focusing on responsibly managing the environmental impact of its daily operations, with an emphasis on reducing carbon emissions, energy and paper consumption, and waste recycling, while fully leveraging improvements in the fuel mix for electricity generation by local power companies. Additionally, the HKMA is establishing a digitalised working environment to enhance efficiency while reducing its carbon footprint. Furthermore, the HKMA recognises the importance of fostering a culture of sustainability and therefore encourages staff to actively adopt sustainable practices through ongoing promotional programmes and activities. Under the primary target of net-zero emissions by 2030, the HKMA has been exploring the use of carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and procuring low-carbon options where possible. In this regard, since 2023, the HKMA has fully offset carbon emissions from air travel by purchasing sustainable aviation fuel and participating in carbon offset programmes. The HKMA will expand its carbon insetting and offsetting programmes to cover all other major carbon emissions. In addition to the above environmental commitments related to physical operations, the HKMA continues to drive the low-carbon transition in the market, from introducing electronic document submission and processing procedures to promoting electronic payments and the recycling of coins back into circulation. The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA's strategies in leading environmental protection, promoting staff well-being, and caring for the community. Under the HKMA's overall institutional risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. To better assess the potential impact of climate change on its operations, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and reviewed their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring business continuity, the HKMA's office design incorporates multiple measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fire, and other emergencies. Additionally, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans, incorporating comprehensive measures that cover not only the office but also communication and computer facilities. The HKMA regularly conducts evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure staff are always prepared to implement response measures. The HKMA also monitors its exposure to transition risks by tracking greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, energy consumption, and paper usage from its own operations. The HKMA's latest climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions related to its own operations for Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 by 2030 or earlier. These targets have been developed with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative methodology. The HKMA uses the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its institutional emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA's main greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect emissions from electricity generated by fossil fuel consumption. As individual supplier data is unavailable, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimate major Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital products) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfill and staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculations for 2023 and 2024 are presented in the "Performance Summary" on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and basis of this verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" appended to this report. The HKMA leads by example, adhering to the same climate-related standards it expects from the banks it supervises and the financial system it monitors. As a first step towards green commuting, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this effort in 2025 to achieve full green commuting. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in various renovation projects in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and renovation materials or traded in old items for new ones to reduce waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and conservation measures in its offices and data centres. In the 2024 data centre facility upgrade project, the HKMA adopted a modular uninterruptible power supply system to further optimise the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus certified data centre. This design allows for flexible capacity expansion, improves operational efficiency under partial loads, and is equipped with advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping to reduce overall energy consumption. The HKMA enhances internal virtual collaboration through a digital workplace, streamlining workflows and effectively reducing paper usage. Additionally, the HKMA extends the service life of mobile and desktop devices in line with manufacturers' software update cycles, thereby prolonging the secure usage period of the devices. To reduce waste generated in the office, the HKMA follows the "4R" principles—Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle—and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The HKMA has placed recycling bins in multiple convenient locations in the office for recycling different materials. To improve recycling rates, the HKMA added recycling bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit netting in 2024. Furthermore, since November 2022, the HKMA has been sending collected food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA participated in the Environmental Protection Department's "Event Waste Reduction Pledge," committing to take measures to reduce waste generated from various activities. The HKMA continues to prioritise the procurement of goods that meet the environmental specifications of the government's "Green Procurement List," particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to carefully plan itineraries, such as consolidating multiple trips when attending overseas events. At the institutional level, since 2023, the HKMA has been purchasing sustainable aviation fuel to reduce approximately 10% of its annual carbon emissions from air travel. Additionally, the HKMA participates in Gold Standard certified carbon offset programmes to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; these programmes focus on renewable energy production and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged various learning activities for staff, such as seminars and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. From Earth Day on 22 April 2024 through the entire month of May, the HKMA held its first "HKMA Green Month" with the theme "Think Green, Live Green, Work Green." This was a good opportunity to demonstrate the HKMA's commitment and drive to implement environmental sustainability in its internal operations. The activities included a "Sustainability BINGO Scorecard" to encourage staff to adopt a green lifestyle, a "Save the Earth" quiz, and a "Kokedama" indoor plant care workshop originating from Japan; it also shared waste audit results and introduced best practices for recycling by a community recycling centre operator. To sustain the momentum of "Green Month," the HKMA launched a recycling campaign in October lasting approximately six months, highlighting responsible waste management and reminding staff that consolidating small changes in individual habits can significantly enhance the overall recycling performance of the institution. A highlight of the campaign was the launch of a "Green Action" video featuring several senior managers sharing recycling tips. The campaign also introduced a series of screensavers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles, and electronic reminders to encourage staff to reduce waste and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to gauge their understanding of sustainability and gather their views on proposed green office measures. The survey results will help inform the development of future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong's central banking institution, the HKMA sees itself as a key agent of change and is therefore committed to leading the acceleration of the low-carbon transition, promoting sustainable practices within the financial industry and the wider community. The HKMA has launched several measures to enhance the efficiency of external processes. Following the successful launch of the Common Data Submission Platform in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform's service scope in 2024 to cover non-bank institutions, such as stored value facility operators, to facilitate their submission of certain regulatory data. The aim of expanding the platform's service scope is to further streamline the submission process for reporting institutions, providing a smoother experience for all users while reinforcing the HKMA's commitment to sustainability. Other new initiatives launched in 2024 include the SurveyTool, which allows banks to respond to HKMA surveys using a simplified submission process, and a smart information and document management system, providing users with a central platform for advanced search of bank-related documents.

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) has conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (the "Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The Data includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and GHG emissions from air travel for 2024, along with their respective intensities. In addition, the Data also includes Scope 3 GHG emissions from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and employee commuting for 2023 and 2024, together with their corresponding intensities. The HKMA's GHG emissions data has been prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (the "GHG Protocol"), jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covers a total of 6 office and warehouse assets, of which 5 offices are located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, 5) The Cullinan Towers, and the warehouse is at 6) Roxy Industrial Centre, Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, HKQAA reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 6 assets. This verification engagement was performed in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to obtain a reasonable level of assurance for forming an opinion and conclusion. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to its source, and also reviewed and performed reliability tests on the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanism, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the data, and examining selected representative data and information. Relevant source data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the Data. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The HKQAA verification team did not participate in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance on the Data and concludes that: - The Data is materially accurate and reliable; - The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shen Xiaoyin Review Manager Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2025
